idea-plugin.name: DeepSeek Harness Bridge
idea-plugin.description:
Docks the DeepSeek Harness Web UI into a JetBrains IDE tool window and attaches it to the already running desktop build, so the IDE and the desktop window share one backend: same sessions, same workspaces, same credentials.

How it works

The desktop shell keeps its browser launch token in memory, so no second process can guess the URL. A small DSH side plugin writes the authenticated URL to %LOCALAPPDATA%\dsh-ide-bridge\bridge.json; this plugin reads that file, verifies the recorded process is alive, probes the endpoint, and loads it. When the desktop build restarts, the token rotates and the panel reconnects automatically.

Requirements

  • IntelliJ Platform 2026.2+ with JCEF
  • The DeepSeek Harness desktop build running (it is not launched from the IDE)
  • The DSH side bridge plugin installed in that build's profile

Fallback

Before the DSH side plugin is installed, set -Ddsh.web.url=<url printed by dsh web> in Help | Edit Custom VM Options to connect manually.

Forked from github.com/Chocomintopia/dsh-jetbrains-plugin (MIT).
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.0.3

  • Filled buttons (send, Act/Plan, approval) now use the theme's default-button colors and label instead of the link color, so high-contrast themes no longer paint black-on-fluorescent-green controls.

1.0.2

  • The IDE panel now follows the actual IDE theme — Islands, Darcula, IntelliJ Light, High Contrast and custom themes — by sampling the live look-and-feel colors instead of guessing light/dark.
  • Theme and editor color scheme changes apply to an open panel immediately.
  • The panel uses the IDE UI font and editor font family, and gets a stronger focus ring under high-contrast themes.

1.0.1

  • After the desktop build restarts and the token rotates, the tool window returns to the compact IDE panel instead of the full Web UI.
  • The compact panel now streams output live and shows permission prompts from the DSH side plugin.

1.0.0

  • Attaches to the running desktop instance via a hand-off file instead of a static URL.
  • Detects a dead desktop process, a rotated token, and an unreachable port.
  • Reconnects automatically when the desktop build restarts.
  • Keeps the pinned DeepSeek Chat tab and the no-restart reload action.
